extracted.intended_audience: individual donors and philanthropists seeking high-impact, evidence-backed charities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for donors on choosing charities that deliver high impact, based on evidence, cost-effectiveness, geography, and operational characteristics. The page lists recommended organisations and filters (tax status, countries, currencies) used to surface those recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highly effective, evidence-backed interventions with maximum impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Our recommended charities are carefully selected through our rigorous research and evaluation to ensure your donation supports only highly effective, evidence-backed interventions with maximum impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the site's primary selection principle: charities must demonstrate that their interventions are effective and supported by evidence; preferred interventions deliver the largest measurable improvements per dollar or per unit of effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous research and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected through our rigorous research and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charities are evaluated using an internal evaluation framework (see 'Explore Our Alumni Charities' and 'evaluation framework' references). Organisations that no longer align with the current evaluation framework may be listed as alumni rather than active recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax-deductible status
rubrics_metrics.description: Filter by: Tax deductible status / Donations are tax-deductible in the country selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Donors can filter charities by whether donations will be tax-deductible in their selected country; transactional guidance notes which country currencies/tax situations apply to each charity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic scope / Where they operate
rubrics_metrics.description: Where They Operate (long list of countries) — charities are described with the countries or regions where they operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charities are filtered and presented by the countries in which they work; donors should consider the charity's operational geography and whether it serves the intended location/population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness / low-cost interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Charities and programs are described as 'extremely cost-effective' or 'low-cost health interventions' where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference is given to interventions that deliver large benefits at low cost (e.g., Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention described as 'extremely cost-effective'). Cost-effectiveness is a key evaluative dimension for recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability / ability to reach large audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on programs that scale to reach large audiences (e.g., mass media campaigns, programs that 'improve the wellbeing of hundreds of millions').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charities that can operate at scale or use channels that reach broad populations (media campaigns, government partnerships) are highlighted as high-impact options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear measurable outcomes and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of quantitative outputs to illustrate impact (e.g., 'restored sight to more than 2.5 million people', 'delivering a basic income to 20,000+ people', 'more than 200 million doses of antibiotics').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations favour organisations that report concrete, verifiable outputs and outcome metrics; donors are shown numerical evidence of past impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly defined target populations / beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Each charity entry specifies target beneficiaries (e.g., 'girls and boys aged 11 to 24', 'children under 5', 'out-of-school girls', 'smallholder African farmers', 'ultra-poverty households').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective programmes have well-defined beneficiary groups and interventions targeted to those groups; this clarity informs impact estimates and appropriateness for donor goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships with governments and local actors
rubrics_metrics.description: Many charities partner with government and local stakeholders (e.g., 'they partner with the government', 'partners with local governments and communities', 'works with Ministries of Health and Education').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working through or with government and local systems is presented as a strength for scaling, sustainability, and reach; evaluation looks favorably on credible government/local partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability and local capacity-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on activities that build local capacity and sustainability (e.g., 'training doctors and health workers', 'local volunteers who mobilize parents and communities', 'sustainable co-investment model').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program features that increase local ownership, capacity, and long-term resilience are considered positive indicators of lasting impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention specificity and evidence-based program types
rubrics_metrics.description: Charities are evaluated by the specific interventions they deliver (examples include insecticide-treated nets, unconditional cash transfers, deworming, vitamin A supplementation, seasonal malaria chemoprevention, conditional cash incentives for vaccination, school feeding, eye surgery, entrepreneurship training).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference is given to concrete, well-studied intervention types with evidence of effect rather than vague or diffuse activities; the page lists program types as part of the justification for recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about donation processing and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Donations are tax-deductible in the country selected. Credit card donations attract a service fee. To avoid fees see our other ways to donate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site informs donors about payment options, fees, and ways to avoid fees — transactional transparency is part of their stewardship and donor-facing criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with current evaluation framework (alumni status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore Our Alumni Charities — some previously recommended charities may no longer align with our current criteria. While they’re no longer on our active list, these Alumni Charities have made meaningful contributions and may still align with your personal giving values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charities can be moved to an 'alumni' list if they no longer satisfy the evolving evidence-based criteria; continued support is left to donor discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation and program development
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence Action’s Accelerator drives new program development, refining high-potential and cost-effective interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for organisations that test, refine, and scale high-potential interventions is valued; evidence of program development capability is a positive evaluative signal.
